title: Hiragana Reading Check
concept: Recall all basic hiragana by shape and sound

questions.prompt: Match each hiragana to its learner romaji before checking the answer.
questions.explanation: Active matching checks whether the character shape retrieves its sound without relying on chart position.

questions.prompt: Match the t-row and n-row hiragana to their learner romaji.
questions.explanation: Remember the irregular sound labels chi and tsu while keeping the other row sounds predictable.

questions.prompt: Match each h-row or m-row hiragana to its learner romaji.
questions.explanation: Compare the full shapes and crossings; do not identify a character from only one shared stroke.

questions.prompt: Match the final-row hiragana to their learner romaji.
questions.explanation: The y-row has only ya, yu, and yo; ん is the only basic kana that represents a consonant by itself.

questions.prompt: Which reading matches the hiragana word ねこ?
questions.explanation: ね is ne and こ is ko, so the word is neko, cat.

questions.prompt: Which hiragana spelling reads yama, mountain?
questions.explanation: や is ya and ま is ma. Read from left to right: ya-ma.

questions.prompt: Which character is ru and ends with a small loop?
questions.explanation: る closes with a small loop, while ろ keeps the corresponding lower curve open.

questions.prompt: Which character is ki and has two horizontal crossings?
questions.explanation: き has two short horizontal strokes; さ has one crossing near the top.
